summary: 100-foot MC-39 Aermotor tower in Crenshaw County, built 1948 by the Forestry Commission; removed before April 2019, with a March 2013 dismantling also reported.

facts.status_note: NHLR and former-site listing say removed before April 2019; Forest Lookouts says dismantled and shipped to New York in March 2013

access.note: No standing tower is recorded at the site

events.note: Forest Lookouts: dismantled and shipped to New York to be restored and placed at a new location
NHLR and former-site listing: removed prior to April 2019
Former-site photo shows the tower foundation, January 2024

evidence.supports: administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission
built in 1948 by the Forestry Commission
evidence.quote: built in 1948 by the Forestry Commission
was a 100' MC-39 Aermotor with a 7'x7' cab

evidence.supports: once the only remaining fire tower in Crenshaw County
evidence.quote: Once the only remaining fire tower in Crenshaw County
The tower was removed prior to April 2019.
It was removed prior to April 2019.

evidence.supports: dismantled and shipped to New York for restoration and relocation
evidence.quote: The tower was dismantled and shipped to New York where the structure will be restored and placed at a new location.

corrections.why: NHLR and the former-site listing both say the tower was removed prior to April 2019; the foundation was photographed in January 2024

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts gives a March 2013 dismantling and shipment to New York; NHLR and the former-site listing give removal prior to April 2019. Both dates are kept and the story says the accounts differ.

notes_for_editor: No staffing, fire or access sources found. A WebSearch returned a 2013 Greenville Advocate item about a Crenshaw County fire tower being taken down and shipped to New York; the page returned HTTP 403 and the snippet does not name Luverne, so it is not used. It may describe this tower; the Alabama Forestry Commission or the Greenville Advocate archive could confirm. Brief's status 'standing' is wrong: NHLR and FFLOS both say removed. Brief's elevation 136.9 m matches NHLR 449 ft (137 m).
